summary: Iter188 tested pay-with-crypto, the $75 eSIM price, eSIM auto-renew and Texting paused renew, on both backend and frontend (DRY_RUN preview). Backend: 33 of 34 pytest checks passed. The new file is test_crypto_autorenew_iter188.py; the iter186 and iter187 files ran without ESIM_SEND_REAL_TEXT. The one failure is a real bug: if auto-renew is off and the line is suspended, the 15-second biller still takes $75 and turns the line back on. Frontend: every requested flow works end to end. /app/esim CryptoPay goes open → panel → address → deposit with the preview warning, and the Pay button reads $75. In the landing checkout, Alice sees both pay-wallet and use-crypto; use-crypto shows 'Send $75 in crypto…' and the deposit card, and no order was placed after waiting 18 s (one poll). A new account goes straight to topup. Texting: the new setup shows texting-crypto next to 'Pay $200 from wallet' and works through to the deposit card. A paused standalone item (temporary TEST DB row) shows Renew $50 from the wallet and texting-renew-crypto with $50. The auto-renew switch works off → reload keeps it off → on. A simulated line was cancelled through the confirm dialog. Spanish works for the switch, the toast and the crypto panel. es_69fcb8db0c34 was not touched.

critical.issue: Auto-renew off is ignored when a line is suspended. billOne only expires lines where autoRenew===false && status==='active'. A suspended line with autoRenew=false still gets debited $75 on the next tick as soon as the wallet has funds, and goes back to active. Reproduced: test_suspended_with_autorenew_off_not_charged showed status active and a $75 debit. The customer is charged even though they turned auto-renew off.

minor.issue: The 'wallet needs $X' error comes back without code 'insufficient_balance', so the status is 400, not 402. hosted-sms renew does set the code.
custPlan carrier is now 'T-Mobile network'. The iter186/187 tests expected 'US network'; I updated them, assuming the change was intentional.

issues: Once the CryptoPay deposit card shows, it sits inside the flex-wrap button row. With the default align-items:stretch, the 'Pay $X from wallet' and 'Cancel' buttons stretch to the full height of the deposit card. Add items-start to the row, or render the panel/deposit on its own full-width row.
When the panel opens (w-full), the Cancel button wraps under the crypto panel, away from the Pay button.
The amount reads '$75.00 in BTC': the word 'in' is not translated (the template string is built outside i18n).
The header still says '$75/month · next <date>'. It should say 'ends <date>' so the customer knows the line will stop.

action_items: spenza.js billOne: if d.autoRenew === false, expire the line whether it is active or suspended. Explicit renew() from a suspended line should still work: either debit directly in renew, or turn autoRenew back on first.
Fix the CryptoPay layout inside the BuyForm and Texting NewSetup button rows (items-start / separate row).
Optional: translate the 'in' in the '$X in COIN' deposit amount; show the 'ends <date>' wording when auto-renew is off; return 402 from esim renew when the wallet is short.
critical_code_review_comments: spenza.js billOne ignores autoRenew=false for suspended lines (confirmed by test).

In BuyForm and NewSetup, CryptoPay is rendered only while the IMEI/phone check is valid. If the user edits the IMEI or phone after creating a deposit, the component unmounts: the deposit card and the auto-order watcher are lost, and the money stays in the wallet with no order placed.
CryptoPay and the landing Pay both place the order when ANY balance rise after the deposit is created reaches the price (including unrelated credits). That is acceptable, but worth knowing.
setAutoRenew allows status 'provisioning', but the UI only shows the switch on active and suspended lines. That is consistent but not documented.

rca of the issue: billOne(d) starts with `if (d.autoRenew === false && d.status === 'active') return expire(d)`. tick() picks up both active and suspended lines whose nextBillAt <= now. A suspended line keeps its old nextBillAt, so it is retried on every tick, skips the expire branch and calls S.w.debit(price). Repro: buy a simulated line, set status=suspended, autoRenew=false, nextBillAt in the past, wait 15–30 s: $75 is debited and status becomes active. Fix: expire whenever autoRenew===false inside the tick path, and keep the explicit renew() path separate.
